headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: Open Interpreter can execute local code/files while OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API surfaces that can ingest or act on its outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter reads/writes the filesystem and clipboard, and OpenMetadata exposes MCP/API/webhook surfaces. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pair is not documented as directly integrated, so this is inferred from their exposed surfaces rather than observed behavior.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter copies untrusted file or clipboard content into prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF OpenMetadata ingests Open Interpreter output through MCP, APIs, or webhooks without provenance checks, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Require provenance tags on all OpenMetadata inputs.
Use a read-only staging file for any exchanged text.
Turn off MCP/webhook ingestion for untrusted content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can access the entire local filesystem at the user's privilege, including secrets, and has broad network egress. OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory data and can receive data via APIs/webhooks/MCP. If Open Interpreter forwards local files or context into OpenMetadata, sensitive local data can leave the machine without a built-in boundary.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is pointed at directories containing secrets or regulated data, leakage risk is present.
IF OpenMetadata is configured to accept those inputs over API, webhook, or MCP, the data can be exfiltrated into its backend.
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a dedicated non-sensitive workspace.
Block outbound network egress except to approved endpoints.
Disable API/webhook ingestion for sensitive datasets.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and allowlisted sinks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter has filesystem write and git-state modification, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem. OpenMetadata can also operate through APIs/SDKs/events/webhooks, so both agents can mutate shared resources without an explicit locking mechanism. Concurrent writes to the same workspace or metadata targets can overwrite each other or corrupt state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository, directory, or metadata backend, write conflicts can occur.
IF OpenMetadata writes through APIs while Open Interpreter edits the same files or git state, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state.
Use git branches or transactional APIs for all mutations.
Add manual approval before commits or API writes.
requires-engineering: implement locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can generate code, shell commands, and file edits, while OpenMetadata can consume API/event/webhook inputs and is oriented around governance and lineage workflows. If OpenMetadata treats Open Interpreter output as authoritative, mistakes or hallucinations can cascade into downstream metadata changes, reports, or operational actions with no verification step.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Open Interpreter-produced facts without validation, errors can propagate.
IF Open Interpreter emits fabricated lineage or governance details, OpenMetadata may persist them as trusted metadata.
mitigations: Require human review before OpenMetadata writes.
Validate Open Interpreter outputs against source systems.
Mark all imported fields as untrusted until checked.
Limit Open Interpreter to draft-only generation.
requires-engineering: add schema and provenance validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Open Interpreter touches anything reachable on the local machine and can send data to configured model providers, while OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory data through APIs/webhooks/MCP. The pair can therefore move sensitive or regulated data into different retention and residency regimes, but the profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by Open Interpreter and then forwarded into OpenMetadata, retention and access policies must align.
IF the two systems have different logging or deletion policies for the same dataset, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Classify data before passing it between agents.
Disable logging for regulated fields where possible.
Use separate retention policies per dataset.
Document residency and deletion requirements.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement and audit trails.
